venue.name: Strathcona Park Lodge and Outdoor Education Centre
venue.description: Strathcona Park Lodge is a 160 acre off grid outdoor education centre on the shore of Upper Campbell Lake, 5 km before the Buttle Lake entrance to Strathcona Provincial Park and about an hour and a quarter from Courtenay. It has run outdoor education programs since 1959 and takes schools from March to the end of June and again from September to the beginning of November. Schools book either a single day program or a residential week built from canoeing, kayaking, hiking, rock climbing, high ropes, the zipline, camp skills and a night or more camping out. Prices are set per participant and include meals, accommodation and instruction, but no figure is published anywhere on the site.
venue.address: 41040 Gold River Hwy P.O. Box 2160, Campbell River, BC Canada, V9W 5C5

facility_notes.washrooms: Our bathrooms are gender inclusive, our bathing spaces are private.
facility_notes.lunch_space: The Whale Room restaurant serves three meals per day at set times, and meals are included in the program price.

venue.nearby_park: Our Lodge is located 5 km before the Buttle Lake entrance to Strathcona Provincial Park.
restrictions: All participants must sign a waiver and release agreement prior to taking part in an SPL experience or activity.
Minor participants (children 18 and under) must have an Acknowledgment of Risks and Consent Form completed and signed by a parent or guardian.
There is no cellphone reception on property and we do not have internet access for youth while they are here.
Your arrival time should be between 1:00pm - 2:30pm. Please do not arrive early.
Medical forms, youth consent forms, rooming list and group list are required back two weeks before the program start date.
venue.seasonal_notes: Typically, schools join us from March to the end of June and again in September through to the beginning of November.

programs.name: Day Program
programs.description: A single day at the lodge for a school group, drawn from the same activity list as the residential weeks. They describe exploring the lake by canoe, learning about local flora and fauna on the trails, practising wilderness skills and building trust on the high ropes course. No price, age range, group size, start time or finish time is published. Everything is quoted after an email.
programs.what_children_do: Paddle a canoe on the lake, walk the trails looking at the plants and animals of coastal British Columbia, try wilderness skills, or work through the high ropes course together.
programs.our_note: This is the only option here that does not involve a night away, which makes it the realistic one for a younger group. Nothing about it is priced or age limited on the site, so make your first email ask what the youngest children they take are and what a day costs for each child.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and a restaurant are on site, and the property is 160 acres of trails, beaches and lakefront. Step free access, rain backup and bus parking are not covered anywhere on the site, so it is worth a call.
programs.evidence: These programs are great for schools looking for a fun way to increase teamwork, an educational trip to boost curriculum, or a class celebration.

programs.name: Adventure Program, 4 or 5 days
programs.description: Their most common school week and a 4 or 5 day residential stay. It introduces canoeing, kayaking, rock climbing, high ropes, the zipline, the bog walk, camp skills and orienteering, and includes a one night out trip on Buttle Lake where the group sleeps under one shared tarp. Groups arrive at 1pm on the first day and leave at 9am on the last. One lodge instructor is provided for every 10 students, plus a teacher or chaperone. They recommend planning a year ahead.
programs.what_children_do: Paddle a canoe or kayak, climb a rock face and rappel down it, cross a high ropes course, ride the zipline, walk the bog trail, then carry their kit out for a night of camping, cooking on a fire and sleeping under one shared tarp with the rest of the group.
programs.our_note: This is a week away from home for children old enough to sleep out under a tarp, not a day trip. The price is per participant and covers meals, a bed and instruction, and the trip coordinator goes free, but no figure is published, so the quote is the only way to find out.
programs.practical_summary: Meals, beds and washrooms are all on site and included in the price. There is no phone signal and no internet for young people, and nothing is published about step free access or bus parking.
programs.payment_timing: A 25% non-refundable deposit is due within 30 days of the invoice date to confirm your reservation. The invoice remainder is due on arrival.
programs.cancellation_note: Cancellations with more than 3 months' notice will forfeit the deposit. If SPL is able to fill the booking dates with another school booking, a full or partial refund, subject to a $100 administration fee, will be provided. Cancellations with less than 3 months' notice will forfeit the deposit.
programs.evidence: Our Adventure programs include 1 SPL instructor per 10 students plus a teacher/chaperone.

programs.name: Specialty Program, one activity for the week
programs.description: A week immersed in a single activity, with 2 to 3 nights camping out. The choices published for 2026 are an introductory or intermediate hike, the Brewster Lakes and Sayward Forest canoe portage route, ocean canoeing from Mutchalat Inlet, sea kayaking in Nootka Sound, whitewater kayaking or canoeing on the Campbell or Gold River, rock climbing at Crest Creek Crags, wilderness skills, mountain biking, a rock and cave combination, and a Buttle Lake canoe trip. Two lodge instructors are provided for every 10 students and a teacher or chaperone is optional.
programs.what_children_do: Learn one skill properly and then travel with it. Depending on the choice they paddle a sea kayak for two to six hours at a stretch, portage a canoe up to 2 km, rappel down a 20 metre rock face, crawl through caves, or ride a mountain bike for three to six hours a day, sleeping under a tarp for two or three nights.
programs.our_note: These are expedition weeks for young people who are already fit and comfortable outdoors. Some routes have no outhouses at all. Ask which trips they can actually run on your dates, because the choice moves with water levels and the time of year.
programs.practical_summary: Gear, meals and special diets are all handled by the lodge. Camping out means no washrooms on some nights, and nothing is published about step free access or bus parking.
programs.payment_timing: A 25% non-refundable deposit is due within 30 days of the invoice date to confirm your reservation. The invoice remainder is due on arrival.
programs.cancellation_note: Cancellations with more than 3 months' notice will forfeit the deposit. If SPL is able to fill the booking dates with another school booking, a full or partial refund, subject to a $100 administration fee, will be provided. Cancellations with less than 3 months' notice will forfeit the deposit.

chaperone_ratio.applies_to: Specialty Programs, where a teacher or chaperone is optional

programs.evidence: Our Specialty Programs include 2 SPL instructors per 10 students (a teacher/chaperone is optional).

programs.name: Custom program for a youth organization
programs.description: Programs built with groups that are not schools. They name community groups, First Nations youth, Scouts and Guides, international groups, sports teams and arts organisations, and say these run from a one day activity up to a three week camp, covering camps, retreats, team building and expeditions. Enquiries go to the general office address with the group's size and ages, preferred dates and goals.
programs.what_children_do: It depends what is agreed. They describe camps, retreats, team building and outdoor expeditions, drawn from the same activity list as the school programs.
programs.our_note: This is the door for a group that is not a school, and it is the only place on the site that says a single day is possible. It is also the only place that asks for your ages, so put them in the first email and you will find out quickly whether your children are old enough.
programs.practical_summary: Same site as the school programs, with meals, beds and washrooms on the property. Price, youngest age and group size are all unpublished, so the quote is where they get settled.
programs.evidence: From one-day activities to three-week camps, we work with you to develop the perfect experience for your participants.

gaps: PRICE. No dollar figure appears anywhere on this site for any school program, day or residential. All they publish is that pricing is on a per participant basis that includes meals, accommodation and instructional activities, and that the trip coordinator joins for free. A residential week here is a per student price for the whole stay rather than a nightly rate, but the amount only comes with their quote, so budget nothing until you have it in writing.

AGES AND GRADES. Not published. Nothing on the school programs page, the youth programs page, the activities page or the youth questions page gives a minimum age, a grade range or a youngest age welcomed for a school group. Their summer camps are advertised for ages 12 to 17, but those are individually booked expeditions, not the school programs. For a daycare or a primary class this is the first question to ask.

HOW MANY ADULTS HAVE TO COME: this is our reading, not their rule. Their school programs page says Adventure programs include one lodge instructor per 10 students plus a teacher or chaperone, and Specialty programs include two instructors per 10 students with a teacher or chaperone optional. We have recorded one adult per ten children from those two lines, but they are written as instructor ratios, not as a stated policy on how many of your own adults must travel. Confirm it before you count heads.
Group size: no minimum or maximum per booking is published. They mention up to 180 students on the property in a week, which is the whole site rather than one school.
Whether chaperones and teachers pay, and how much, is not stated. Only the trip coordinator is named as going free.
How long a day program runs, and what time it starts and finishes, is not published. Residential groups are asked to arrive between 1:00pm and 2:30pm and leave at 9am on the last day.
Minimum notice to book is not stated. Planning a year in advance is a recommendation, and they say it is never too late to ask about space or the waitlist.

Step free access, stroller access and bus parking are not mentioned anywhere on the site. The property is 160 acres of gravel paths, trails and beaches, and the accommodation is spread through the forest.

Two different general enquiry addresses appear: info@strathconaparklodge.com in the footer of every page, and info@strathconaparklodge.ca on their general questions page. The .com one is on far more pages.

Several of the forms linked from their 2026 school pages are still labelled 2025, including the chaperone welcome letter, the youth consent form, the adult waiver and the medical form. The program descriptions and packing lists are 2026.

COORDINATES: their footer address links to a shortened map link rather than a published pin, so the point here was geocoded. It lands on the lodge on the Gold River Highway, not on the P.O. box in Campbell River that the postal address gives.
IMAGES: none of the photographs on this site carry alt text, so every description here was written after opening the picture and looking at it.

conflicts.note: Two of their pages give different addresses for the person who books school programs. If one bounces, try the other, or ring the lodge. We use the one from their school programs page.
